notes: Quo warranto forfeiture-of-charter action against a railway for an unlawful sale/consolidation to a foreign railway; no occupancy or lodging issue. Selector match ('right-to-lease-12') hit on unrelated corporate consolidation authority citation.
Condemnation/waiver dispute over a railway right of way taken without payment; no dwelling occupancy or lodging issue. 'Incidents of ownership' language refers to land title, not letting practice.
Trespass to try title between tenants in common (heirs) and a railway that purchased a homestead lot; dispute is about co-tenant possession/partition procedure, not compensated lodging.

Interstate commerce / police power case about a statutory penalty for a railway's refusal to deliver freight on tender of bill-of-lading charges. No occupancy or lodging issue; 'police power' matter is freight regulation, not boarding-house regulation.

holding_summary: In a homestead-exemption dispute, the court held that when an owner permanently devotes part of his town homestead lot to houses built and rented out for income, that portion ceases to be exempt homestead, even though the parcel was never formally subdivided; the owner's undisputed practice of renting rooms/houses to a boarding-house keeper and then to a succession of monthly tenants was treated throughout as an ordinary, unquestioned exercise of ownership.

quotes.text: In 1879 he built another residence on the east part of the property, which he testified he built for the purpose of leasing it to tenants for the income to be derived therefrom.
Soon after I bought I sold a lot off the east end of the block to Mrs. Armstead, and after that I sold off to A. A. Barnes a lot off the west end of the block

notes: Marginal call: the actual holding is homestead-abandonment doctrine, not the legality/character of letting itself. Included because the owner's practice of renting his old residence to a boarding-house keeper (he then boarded with her) and building a second house purely to rent for income is never questioned as unlawful -- courts treat it as an unremarkable incident of ownership, only debating its homestead consequence. Court never classifies the arrangement as lease/license/lodging, so characterization left null. 'boarded with her' is an existing lexicon term, not new.

Injunction/setoff dispute over an estate's judgment; the underlying unliquidated claim happens to arise from a breached covenant to deliver a multi-year hotel lease (Grand Windsor Hotel) and furniture, but the opinion addresses only injunction and setoff procedure, never the character of the hotel occupancy itself. Passing mention only.
Partition-jurisdiction dispute among tenants in common of undivided land interests; purely a venue/joinder question, no dwelling occupancy or lodging issue.

Trespass/joint-trespasser damages case over forcible repossession of a rented bed and pillows under a weekly chattel-rental contract kept in the plaintiff's own residence. This is a personal-property (chattel) rental, not a letting of rooms/dwelling space; no lodging or boarding issue.
Riparian water-rights and license-to-dam-a-stream dispute between adjoining landowners; the 'license' discussed is a water-use easement, not a lodging/room letting. No occupancy issue.

Trespass to try title concerning a mortgagee-in-possession dispute over San Antonio lots; a tenant (Cadwallader) pays rent to the true owner while title is in a mortgagee's name, but this is ordinary landlord-tenant background to a mortgage-priority fight, not a lodging/boarding issue.

Business partners in a drug store; one partner's family occupied the upper story of the building by the other partner's (the owner's) consent as part of their partnership arrangement, not for separate compensation. Court held this was joint occupancy incident to the partnership, not a landlord-tenant/lodging relationship -- outside the corpus's compensated-occupancy focus.

Forcible-detainer pleading/proof case turning on whether a landlord-tenant relationship was adequately alleged and proven; purely a pleading-sufficiency holding with no facts about lodging or boarding arrangements.

Dispute over forcible taking/detention of household goods and farm property between a landowner and a farm occupant; concerns care/return of chattels, not the legal character of the occupancy itself. No lodging issue.
Boundary-line/adverse-possession title dispute; admissibility of declarations of tenants in possession offered to prove limitation, but no lodging or boarding-house facts.

Damages action against a landowner for willfully leasing adjoining premises to prostitutes for purposes of prostitution, creating a nuisance to a neighboring homeowner. Concerns tortious liability of a landlord for a tenant's nuisance use, not the legal character or regulation of lodging/boarding-house letting; outside corpus scope.

Trespass to try title turning on constructive-tenancy/attornment estoppel doctrine and a dormant-judgment execution sale; the successive tenants (Adams/Dunn/Brown/Tatum) occupy an urban lot under ordinary leases, not lodging/boarding arrangements, and the issue litigated is title estoppel, not letting doctrine.

Injunction dispute between two street-railway companies over an exclusive right-of-way easement to a union depot; 'incident of ownership' language concerns a railroad's power to dedicate or grant easements over its own land, unrelated to dwelling occupancy.

Land-title dispute resting on five/ten-year limitation claims and the preclusive effect of a judgment against a tenant; the 'landlord' discussed is a title-claimant, not a lodging-house operator. No occupancy-for-pay issue.
